description: Machine-readable catalog of the tools a grab-mcp server exposes. Each entry maps to a grab CLI verb. `annotations` are standard MCP ToolAnnotations (readOnlyHint follows MCP semantics — writing an output file counts as modifying the environment). `x-grab-category` is grab's own classification and is what a server's --read-only mode / allowlist should gate on: observe+capture never touch the desktop; window-control and input-synthesis do. `cli` is the base command; a server MUST use explicit per-tool argv adapters (flag renames, mutual-exclusion, value conversion) rather than generating argv from this string. Only doctor, windows, and watch-status emit JSON today; the rest print text and need parsing or a JSON mode added upstream.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Report the available display, backends, and capabilities as JSON. Call first to confirm the desktop session is reachable. Emits JSON.

display.description: X display to probe, e.g. ":0". Passed through the environment; not a grab flag.

tools.name: list_windows
tools.description: List every mapped top-level window with native id, WM_CLASS, title, EWMH type, pid, and screen-coordinate bounds. Emits JSON. Use it to resolve the id/class other tools need.

wm_class.description: --class: keep only windows whose WM_CLASS contains this substring (case-insensitive).

type.description: --type: filter by EWMH window type, e.g. "normal", "dialog".

tools.name: capture_screen

annotations.title: Screenshot a window, output, or region

tools.description: Capture a PNG to `out`. Focus-safe. Provide EXACTLY ONE target: window (--window), window_id (--window-id), output_name (--output), full_display (--display), or region (--region). Prints text, not JSON. A server should also return the PNG as MCP image content, not only the path.

window.description: --window: capture the window whose WM_CLASS matches this substring.

window_id.description: --window-id: capture the window with this native id (e.g. "0x1e00007").

full_display.description: --display: capture the entire display (boolean flag, takes no value).

region.description: --region: capture a region in the form "X,Y,WxH" (note: width and height are joined by 'x').

tools.name: watch_capture
tools.description: Watch a window and write a fresh PNG when it changes. This is a screenshot watcher, NOT an input-event observer (event observation lives in `grab daemon`). Long-running: a server MUST bound it (duration_ms) and support cancellation. Requires both window and out.

window.description: --window: WM_CLASS substring of the window to watch.

out.description: --out: path (or pattern) to write PNGs to.

duration_ms.description: Server-enforced cap: stop after this many milliseconds.

tools.name: compare_images
tools.description: Compare two PNGs (positional A B) and report a match_ratio and diff_pixels count. Prints text, not JSON (there is no --json for compare today). Directory comparison offers an additional RMSE metric.

notify.description: --notify: raise a desktop notification on mismatch.

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run a manifest-driven batch of capture/compare operations. Writes image files. Prints text, not JSON.

tools.name: focus_window
tools.description: Raise and focus a window by WM_CLASS substring or native id. Idempotent (converges on the same end state). Mutates the desktop but does not synthesize pointer/keyboard input. Provide exactly one selector.

window.description: --window: WM_CLASS substring of the window to focus.

window_id.description: --window-id: native id of the window to focus.

tools.name: place_window
tools.description: Drive a window to an exact geometry and poll until it has held it. Clears maximised/fullscreen first. Idempotent. Provide exactly one selector plus geometry.

window.description: --window: WM_CLASS substring of the window to place.

window_id.description: --window-id: native id of the window to place.

geometry.description: --geometry: target as "WxH+X+Y" (the X11 spelling: size then offset; offsets may be negative), e.g. "1280x720+100+100".

timeout_ms.description: --timeout: budget in ms for the window to reach and hold the geometry.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click at screen coordinates (--at) or a resolved UI locator (--locator). Moves the real pointer — never call speculatively; capture_screen first to confirm the target. Provide exactly one of at/locator.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Type a string into the currently focused surface as real keystrokes. Focus the intended window first (focus_window).

tools.name: key
tools.description: Send a single key by X keysym NAME (e.g. "Return", "Escape", "a"), resolved via xkbcommon — NOT a chord string like "ctrl+s". Optionally target a window by class or id; otherwise it goes to the focused surface.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Press, move in a straight line, and release between two screen points. Use drag_curve for gesture/curved drags.

tools.name: drag_curve

annotations.title: Curved / gesture drag within a window

tools.description: Perform a curved drag gesture from src to dst within a window (window-relative gesture recipe). Moves the real pointer.

window.description: --window: WM_CLASS substring of the target window.
